prompts.languages.plan.short: Make a 30-minute [language] lesson plan for level [level].
prompts.languages.plan.detailed: Make a self-study [language] lesson plan. My level: [level]. Topic: [topic]. Time: [minutes] minutes. Split it into blocks: warm-up, new rule or words, exercises, speaking or writing, review. For each block give the time and exactly what to do. No more than 10 new words.
prompts.languages.plan.refine: The plan is too packed. Cut it down so it fits into [minutes] minutes without rushing.
prompts.languages.plan.check: I've done the lesson. Give me 5 short questions to check what I remember about “[topic]”.
prompts.languages.grammar.short: Explain this rule in simple words: [rule] in [language].
prompts.languages.grammar.detailed: Explain the grammar rule [rule] in [language] for level [level]. Structure: when it's used, how it's formed, 5 examples with translation, 2 common mistakes and how to avoid them. Avoid complex linguistic terms; if one is unavoidable, explain it.
prompts.languages.grammar.refine: I still mix up [rule] and [similar rule]. Show the difference with pairs of similar sentences.
prompts.languages.grammar.check: Give me 6 gap-fill sentences on [rule]. Show the answers only after I send mine.
prompts.languages.tenses.short: Give me 10 exercises on the [tenses] tenses in [language].
prompts.languages.tenses.detailed: Make a practice set on the [tenses] tenses in [language] for level [level]. 12 sentences from a student's everyday life: put the verb in the right form, choose an option, translate. First give only the tasks. When I send my answers, check them, explain each mistake in one sentence and give my score.
prompts.languages.tenses.refine: Most of my mistakes are with [tense]. Give 8 more sentences just on it, from easy to hard.
prompts.languages.tenses.check: Here's my story about last weekend: [text]. Find the tense mistakes and explain them.
prompts.languages.words.short: Give me 15 useful [language] words on “[topic]” with translation.
prompts.languages.words.detailed: Make a table of 15 [language] words and phrases on “[topic]” for level [level]. Columns: word, translation, part of speech, a short example sentence, common collocations. Pick words that are actually useful in conversation, not rare ones.
prompts.languages.words.refine: Group these words by meaning and suggest a way to remember each group.
prompts.languages.words.check: Test me: give me the words from the list in my language one by one, and I'll write the translation. Keep score.
prompts.languages.check.short: Check my [language] text and correct the mistakes: [text]
prompts.languages.check.detailed: Check my [language] text. My level: [level]. First list the mistakes: what I wrote, the correct version, why (one sentence). Then give the corrected text, keeping my words and style as much as possible. Don't add new ideas. Text: [text]
prompts.languages.check.refine: Now suggest how to make the text sound more natural, but no harder than level [level].
prompts.languages.check.check: I've corrected the text: [text]. Are there any mistakes left? Mark only those, without rewriting.
prompts.languages.dialogue.short: Let's talk in [language] about [topic]. You ask questions and I'll answer.
prompts.languages.dialogue.detailed: Play a conversation partner in [language] in this situation: [situation]. My level: [level]. Rules: one short line at a time, wait for my reply. If I make a mistake, add the correct version in brackets at the end of your line. After 8 exchanges, end the conversation and list my main mistakes.
prompts.languages.dialogue.refine: Speak more simply: shorter phrases, no idioms, one question at a time.
prompts.languages.dialogue.check: List 5 phrases from our dialogue that I should learn, with an example for each.
prompts.languages.oral.short: Help me prepare a spoken answer in [language] to: [question]
prompts.languages.oral.detailed: Help me prepare a 1–2 minute spoken answer in [language] to “[question]”, level [level]. Give a 4-point plan, 2–3 useful phrases for each point and linking phrases between parts. Don't write a full ready-made text: I want to speak in my own words.
prompts.languages.oral.refine: Add 3 follow-up questions an examiner might ask after my answer, with hints on how to reply.
prompts.languages.oral.check: Here's my answer written down: [text]. Rate coherence, vocabulary and accuracy out of 5 and explain the scores.
prompts.languages.level.detailed: Rewrite the [language] text for level [level]: shorter sentences, common words, no rare idioms. Keep all the facts and the order of ideas. After the text, list 8 difficult words from the original with explanations in simple [language]. Text: [text]
prompts.languages.level.refine: Make another version one level higher so I can work my way up to the original.
prompts.languages.level.check: Ask 5 comprehension questions on the simplified text. Check my answers after I write them.
prompts.languages.mistakes.detailed: My teacher marked mistakes in my [language] sentences: [sentences]. For each, explain: what's wrong, which rule is broken, the correct version. Then find what my mistakes have in common and suggest a topic to practise.
prompts.languages.mistakes.refine: Explain mistake [number] again by comparing it with my native language.
prompts.languages.mistakes.check: Give me 5 new sentences with the same trap so I can check I've understood the rule.
prompts.languages.translate.short: Translate into [language] and explain the tricky parts: [text]
prompts.languages.translate.detailed: Translate the text into [language] for [purpose]. After the translation, give a table: original phrase, how it's translated, why, a possible alternative. Mark places with no exact equivalent where the meaning is only approximated. Text: [text]
prompts.languages.translate.refine: The translation sounds too formal. Make a version for [situation], keeping the meaning.
prompts.languages.translate.check: Here's my own translation: [translation]. Compare it with the original and mark where the meaning changed.

verify.languages.plan: Compare the plan with your textbook or course syllabus: the AI doesn't know what you've already covered.
verify.languages.grammar: Check the rule against a textbook or grammar reference: AI sometimes simplifies to the point of being wrong.
verify.languages.tenses: Some sentences allow two options. If your answer differs, ask why it's wrong rather than just accepting the correction.
verify.languages.words: Check pronunciation and examples in a dictionary: AI may invent unnatural word combinations.
verify.languages.check: Don't rewrite the whole text as the AI suggests: keep your own wording where it's correct.
verify.languages.dialogue: AI is a patient partner but not a native speaker. Check set phrases in a dictionary or with a teacher.
verify.languages.oral: Speak in your own words: memorising someone else's text sounds unnatural in an exam.
verify.languages.level: Compare the simplified text with the original: meaning may have been lost or changed.
verify.languages.mistakes: If the explanation contradicts your textbook, trust the textbook and ask your teacher.
verify.languages.translate: Machine translation isn't suitable for official documents: use a translator. For study, check uncertain words in a dictionary.
